tagline: A season with the players below the stars.

opener: A new season at the old barn. Same boards, same hopes.
First game of the year. Nobody has lost one yet.
The ice is in and the {team} are back. That is enough for tonight.
Opening night. Half the town is here and the other half has the radio on.
Another season. The club is still open, which was not a sure thing.
The zamboni started on the second try. A good omen in {town}.
New tape, old skates. The {team} open tonight.
Somebody painted the lines over the summer. The rest is the same.
The program costs what it cost last year. So does the coffee.
First night. The roster fits on one side of a napkin.
winStreak: {n} wins in a row for the {team}. Nobody is saying it out loud yet.
That is {n} straight. The {town} barn has not been this loud in a while.
{n} in a row. The room is quiet about it, which is the right way to be.
The {team} have won {n} straight and still dress the same six.
{n} wins running. Somebody check the standings twice.
{n} straight. The bus has been quiet in the good way.
The {team} have {n} in a row and nobody has changed his socks.
{n} wins on the trot. The bakery has put a sign in the window.
It is {n} now. Somebody will say the word soon and ruin it.
{n} in a row for {town}. Enjoy it; it never lasts as long as it should.
loseStreak: {n} losses in a row. The {team} will dress tonight all the same.

{n} in a row dropped. The club has seen worse and stayed open.

{n} losses running. The coffee at the rink is still hot.
{n} losses running. The room is short on jokes.
The {team} have dropped {n} straight. The ice is the same size it always was.
{n} in a row the wrong way. Tonight would be a fine night to stop.
It is {n} now. Nobody in {town} is asking for refunds yet.
{n} straight defeats. The coffee is still hot, at least.
lastStrike: One more loss and the season is over. The {team} know it.
No room left: the next loss ends it. Skate accordingly.
The {team} are down to their last strike. Everybody in {town} can count.
Lose tonight and the lights go off until autumn.
Last strike. It has to be tonight and every night after.
One more loss and the season is done. The {team} know the arithmetic.
No room left. The {team} play tonight like the lights depend on it.
This is the edge. Win, and there is a next week.
The {team} have used up their mistakes. Tonight has to be clean.
Last chance for {town}. Bring your voice.
rival: The {rival} again. These two do not need an introduction.
{rival} tonight. Nobody in {town} needs the schedule to know that.
Another night with the {rival}. Bring a second stick.
The {team} and the {rival}. It was never going to be a quiet one.
It is the {rival}. Some games mean more and this is one.
{rival} again. Leave the good china at home.
The {team} and {rival}. The handshake line will be brief.
{rival} are in the building. So is every grudge in {town}.
Nobody needs telling what {rival} means around here.
It is {rival} tonight. The standings are beside the point.
boss: {boss} tonight. {person}, their {role}, has seen clubs like this come and go.
The {team} against {boss}. {person} will have them ready.
{boss}, and {person} with them. A long night's work ahead.
Nobody gave the {team} this game. That has not stopped them before.
{boss} are the measure. {person} is the reason.
{boss} do not lose to clubs like the {team}. That is what {person} was told, anyway.
{person} and {boss} came a long way to be here. The {team} only crossed the parking lot.
The gate will be good tonight. {boss} bring a crowd, and {person} brings the rest.
{boss} tonight. The {team} have a plan, and a goalie, and that is the list.
Ask {person}, their {role}, about small rinks. Then ask again after the game.
broke: Money is tight at the {team}. The club plays tonight; next month is another matter.
The treasurer is not sleeping. The {team} skate anyway.
There is talk about the books. A full barn would help.
The club is short and everybody knows it. Buy a program.
Lean times for the {team}. They have kept the doors open before.
The lights are on tonight. The club would like that noted.
There is a jar by the door. It is not for tips.
The {team} are counting pucks at practice. Not for the drill.
Nobody at the club is buying new tape this month.
The books are thin in {town}. The crowd can fix that faster than the bank.
playoffs: Playoff hockey in {town}. The beards are coming in.
This is what the long winter was for.
The {team} are in. From here every night could be the last one.
Playoffs. The whole season comes down to a few shifts.
Nobody expected the {team} here in October. Here they are.
Playoff hockey in {town}. Somebody found the good bunting.
The {team} are still playing, and half the league is not.
Every shift counts double now. The {team} dress the same six.
The playoffs. Nobody on this club has had a haircut in a month.
Win and play again. That is all the playoffs have ever been.
champions: The banner went up over the summer. Now everyone wants to take it down.
Champions a year ago. That buys nothing tonight.
The {team} raised a banner. The league has not forgotten.
Defending the title. It is harder to keep than to win.
Last year's champions dress tonight. Same room, new target on it.
There is a banner in the rafters with this year on it. It needs dusting already.
Champions. The {team} still carry their own bags.
The title is in the cabinet by the snack bar. The season is out here.
Everybody plays their best game against the champions. Lucky {team}.
A year ago {town} had a parade. Tonight it has a hockey game.
veteran: {player} is {age} and still first on the ice for warm-up.
Another night for {player}. At {age} he counts them.
{player}, {age}, in the lineup. He has forgotten more than most learn.
At {age}, {player} is still here. So is the club.
{player} is {age}. He tapes his stick the way his father did.
They keep asking {player} when he will stop. He is {age} and still dressing.
{player}, {age}, takes the warm-up slowly. He takes the game seriously.
At {age}, {player} knows where the puck is going. Getting there is another matter.
{player} has been here longer than the scoreboard. He is {age}.
rookie: {player} is {age} and playing like he has somewhere to be.
Keep an eye on {player}. {age} years old and already on the sheet.
The kid, {player}, has {goals} this season. Nobody wanted him either.
{player}, {age}, is finding his feet. The room has taken to him.
A {age}-year-old named {player} is turning into something.
{player} is {age} and has {goals}. He still asks where to park.
The kid, {player}, has {goals} now. Somebody tell him it is not always this easy.
{player}, {age} years old, {goals} on the year. His mother has kept every program.
{goals} for {player}, who is {age}. The veterans make him carry the pucks anyway.
At {age}, {player} has {goals} and no idea how hard that is.
hot: {player} has {goals} this season and wants more.
{goals} goals for {player}. He was on waivers a year ago.
{player} leads the {team} with {goals}. He would tell you it is the linemates.
{player}, {goals} on the year. The third line is paying its way.
{player} has {goals} and the goalies have noticed.
{goals} on the year for {player}. Give him the puck and get out of the way.
{player}, {goals} goals. He says the puck is just finding him.
They are checking {player} closer now. That is what {goals} goals buys you.
{goals} and counting for {player}. The net looks big to him lately.
plain: Another night at the rink. The {team} dress six and a goalie, same as always.
A regular night in {town}. Those count too.
The {team} are at it again. Nothing fancy.
Two points on the table and a cold night outside.
Hockey tonight. The club is open and the ice is good.
The {team} skate tonight. That is the whole story so far.
A weeknight in {town}. The regulars are in their seats.
Nothing rides on tonight but two points and somebody's pride.
The {team} play, the organ plays, and the popcorn is fresh.
No story tonight. Just the {team} and sixty feet of ice either way.
cupTie: A cup tie tonight. Lose and the {team} are out of it; win and they are not. Simple game.
The cup. No second chances in it, which is the charm.
Tonight is for the cup. The league can wait a day.
A cup night in {town}. One and done, for somebody.
The {team} have a cup tie. Old silver, small club, long odds.
Cup hockey: win or watch the rest from the stands.
It is a cup tie. The {team} have nothing to lose but the cup.
cupAlive: The {team} are still in the cup, {n} ties down. Nobody is polishing anything yet.
{n} cup ties won. {town} has started to say the word quietly.
Still alive in the cup after {n}. It was not in the budget.
The cup run goes on: {n} won. The trophy cabinet has room.
{n} down in the cup and the {team} are still standing.
A small club, {n} cup ties in. Stranger things have happened, though not here.
cupOut: The cup is gone for another year. The league is still here.
No cup for the {team} this season. They never liked the look of it anyway.
Out of the cup. One less thing to dust.
The cup went the way cups do. The {team} play on.
No more cup ties. The schedule got simpler, if nothing else.
The cup run is over. It was good while {town} had it.
targetNear: One more win and the sponsor's cheque gets bigger. No pressure.
The {team} are a win short of what the sponsor asked for.
The man who pays for the sweaters wants one more win. So does everyone.
One win from keeping a promise. The {team} did not make it, but they will keep it.
The sponsor asked for a number. The {team} are one away.
A win tonight and the treasurer sleeps.
targetMet: The sponsor got what he asked for. Everything from here is extra.
The {team} have done what the sponsor wanted. The cheque will say so.
The target is met. The sign over the door stays up another year.
The man who pays for the sweaters is smiling. It does not happen often.
What was asked of the {team} has been done. Now they play for themselves.
The sponsor is happy, the treasurer is happy, and there is still hockey to play.
nickname: They call {player} "{nick}" now. He pretends not to like it.
"{nick}" is in the lineup. His mother still calls him {player}.
{player}, or "{nick}" to everybody in the building, dresses tonight.
Nobody remembers who first said "{nick}". {player} answers to it now.
"{nick}" tonight. It says {player} on the sheet.
Ask for {player} at the rink and they will ask who. Ask for "{nick}".
newLeague: Welcome to {league}. The rinks are bigger and so is everybody in them.
The {team} are in {league} now. Nobody here knows their names yet.
{league}. The {team} earned the right to be the smallest club in it.
A new league for {town}. The bus rides are longer and the coffee is worse.
First nights in {league}. The {team} brought the same six and a goalie.
{league} does not know what to make of the {team}. That suits the {team}.
twoPlayers: Two hands on the wheel for the {team} this season. It shows.
The {team} have had help this year, and nobody is too proud to say so.
It takes two, some nights. The {team} have had two.
A second pair of eyes behind the bench this season. The {team} look the better for it.
Good company makes a long season shorter. Ask the {team}.
legacy: {player} is behind the bench now. He still reaches for a stick.
{player} hung them up and stayed. The kids listen to him, mostly.
They gave {player} a whistle. He has not put it down.
{player} coaches now. He says it is harder than playing and nobody believes him.
{player} never left the building. The {team} are better for it.
